query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In a face-centered-cubic (FCC) CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) that is initially a single-phase solid solution with equiaxed ~10 µm grains, exposure to diffusible hydrogen during service leads to hydrogen segregation to grain boundaries and stacking-fault tetrahedra. This segregation locally lowers grain-boundary cohesion and promotes nano-void coalescence, so that under monotonic or cyclic tensile loading the alloy fails by inter-granular brittle fracture with at least a 40 % drop in J-integral fracture toughness (J_IC) compared with the hydrogen-free baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA produced by arc-melting, homogenized 48 h/1200 °C, water-quenched, cold-rolled 10 %, recrystallized 1 h/1000 °C → single FCC phase, ~10 µm grains, no second phases, baseline vacuum hydrogen level <0.1 wt ppm.
generation.intervention: Cathodic hydrogen charging in 0.1 M NaOH + 3 g L⁻¹ NH₄SCN at −1.0 V_SCE for 24 h to reach bulk H ≈ 5 wt ppm.
generation.conditions: Room temperature to −150 °C tensile or fracture-toughness tests at strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹ in argon glovebox (<0.1 ppm O₂, H₂O); compare hydrogen-charged vs. uncharged specimens.
generation.structural_mediator: Hydrogen-decorated grain boundaries and stacking-fault tetrahedra that reduce local cohesive strength and act as preferential void-nucleation sites during plastic deformation.
generation.mechanism: Hydrogen lowers the grain-boundary separation energy (Rice–Wang mechanism) and stabilises local partial dislocations, enhancing planar slip. The combination suppresses cross-slip, elevates stress triaxiality at boundaries, and nucleates nano-voids that link up into inter-granular cracks, thus shifting fracture from ductile trans-granular micro-void coalescence to brittle boundary separation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the hydrogen-free baseline, hydrogen-charged samples will show: (1) ≥40 % reduction in J_IC and ≥30 % reduction in Charpy V-notch impact energy; (2) SEM fracture surfaces dominated (>70 %) by flat, faceted inter-granular areas with river patterns; (3) Atom Probe Tomography evidence of >5 at % H at fracture-initiating grain boundaries; (4) No significant change in yield strength (<5 %).
generation.baseline: Uncharged CoCrFeMnNi HEA tested under identical conditions exhibits ~200 kJ m⁻² Charpy energy and ~200 kJ m⁻² J_IC with ductile trans-granular dimple fracture.
generation.boundary: Effect expected when: (a) hydrogen content ≥2 wt ppm, (b) temperature ≤RT (more severe below −50 °C), (c) strain rate between 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻² s⁻¹. Outside this window (e.g., high temperatures >200 °C allowing hydrogen effusion, or very high strain rates >10² s⁻¹ giving limited diffusion time) embrittlement should diminish.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of toughness loss may vary with exact grain size distribution and residual dislocation density; competing mechanisms such as twinning-induced plasticity could partially offset embrittlement at cryogenic temperatures.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two matched sets of compact-tension (C(T)) specimens from the same HEA plate. Subject one set to the specified cathodic hydrogen charging; keep the other in vacuum. Test both sets at −100 °C in an environmental chamber. Post-fracture, perform SEM fractography and 3D atom-probe on boundary regions near the fracture origin.
measurements: Bulk hydrogen content by hot extraction
Fracture-surface morphology and fraction inter-granular vs. trans-granular (SEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If hydrogen-charged samples show (i) less than 10 % reduction in J_IC relative to baseline AND (ii) fracture surfaces remain predominantly trans-granular dimples (<30 % inter-granular area) despite confirmed bulk H ≥2 wt ppm, then the hypothesis is falsified.
